newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-BORG, VILAS RENEW RIVALRY IN PRAGUE ATP SENIOR EVENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BORG, VILAS RENEW RIVALRY IN PRAGUE ATP SENIOR EVENT.

text.p: The ATP European Senior Tour kicked off play on Thursday, with some of the game's greatest names living up to their advance billing, highlighted by a three-set duel between Bjorn Borg and Guillermo Vilas.

The tour, which is looking to capitalise on some of the sport's most recognised personalities, could not have asked for a better start, with local favourite Tomas Smid beating 1990 French Open winner Andres Gomez 4-6 6-4 and 10-8 in the third set, a first to 10 points tiebreak.
Six-time French Open winner Bjorn Borg then followed up with another third-set tiebreak win, beating Argentina's Guillermo Vilas 5-7 6-4 and 10-8 in the third set tiebreak.
"It's always was a tough match with Guillermo, and this was another one," said Borg, who holds 11 Grand Slam titles in total.
Added Vilas: "You can't get a match much closer than 10-8 in the final tiebreak. It really is exciting to be playing again with such great players, and friends."

The ATP men's tour has faced criticism in recent months as being too boring, with rallies lasting no more than three or four hits as serves consistently travel over 200 kmh and players more worried about endorsement contracts than having fun.

With an eye on the booming popularity of the PGA Senior's golf tour, ATP officials are anxious to showcase players that were household names in the 70's and 80's, and harken back to a time when the actual playing time of a match was longer than the breaks in between games.
While the Seniors' tour may appear on the surface to have less of a feel of competitveness, noth players stressed winning still came first.
"We play to win, just as we used to. It's just that now, after the match, we take losing in a different way," said Borg.

Though prize money pales in comparison to regular ATP tournaments -- total purses are set at $125,000 -- points will be awarded and rankings established with an eye on the tour growing from its six tournament schedule this year.
